Chapter 11: Praying for Healing and Restoration
You know, wounds are just part of life. Some you can see, but others—well, they’re hidden deep inside. Illness, heartbreak, betrayal, disappointment... they all leave marks that sometimes linger for years. And for parents, watching your child suffer, there’s this longing—for healing, for restoration, for them to be whole again.
Imagine a son, struggling with depression after a painful breakup. He pulled away from everyone—family, friends—leaving his parents unsure how to help. So, they did what they could: they prayed. They asked for a little light to break through, for hope to sneak back in, for just the right support to cross his path. And over time, with care and patience, he started to heal. His parents realized their prayers were part of the journey—a quiet force working behind the scenes.
Most of us don’t notice how much healing happens in tiny steps. It’s hardly ever instant, or dramatic. Parents hoping for quick fixes often have to learn patience. Trusting that every day brings just a bit more strength—that’s not always easy, but it matters.
There’s also the story of a mother whose daughter carried old wounds from childhood. This mom prayed for forgiveness, for her daughter to let go of bitterness, for the courage to reach out and get help. Over time, her daughter found freedom—she learned to let go and discovered new joy. Watching that, the mother realized: healing really is possible, even when the past feels too heavy to carry.
Restoration—well, it’s more than just fixing what’s broken. It’s about becoming whole again. It’s about peace, and about discovering a new sense of purpose. As parents, you can pray for healing—not just in the body, but in mind and spirit too. For relationships to be mended, for hope to be restored.
And sometimes, those prayers are the very thing that helps turn things around.
